2gdufl8i106: Anomaly policies are enabled by default and rely on user and entity behavior analytics and machine learning. Data from API connectors can take several hours. Risk is assessed on more than 30 indicators grouped into factors (risky IP address, failed sign-ins, administrative activity, inactive accounts, location, impossible travel, device and user agent, activity rate). **Since June 2025**, MDA is migrating to a **dynamic detection model**: several legacy policies (for example activity from suspicious or anonymous IP addresses, suspicious inbox forwarding, ransomware) have been disabled and their coverage taken over by the new model, with no action on your part. 1vn9ekb409j: **Conditional access app control** routes browser sessions to MDA through an Entra ID conditional access policy (“Use Conditional Access App Control”), then applies **access policies** (allow or block) and **session policies** (allow with monitoring, with actions such as blocking the download of sensitive files to unmanaged devices, requiring labeling, blocking the upload of unlabeled files or malware, and re-evaluating conditional access). Policies apply at the **application** level, not the file level. A policy created for a host application (Teams, Exchange) does not cover the linked resource applications (SharePoint, OneDrive): create a separate policy. In Edge, direct in-browser protection applies; in other browsers, the user is redirected through the reverse proxy and sees the `.mcas.ms` suffix. To avoid bypass, block access from native clients. 170jepakwe1: Microsoft Entra ID Protection detects, investigates and remediates identity-based risks. It produces two notions that must be kept distinct. **Sign-in risk** answers “is this sign-in probably made by the real owner of the account?” and is calculated at each sign-in. **User risk** answers “is this account probably compromised?” and accumulates over time. A detection can be **real time** (evaluated during the sign-in) or **offline** (calculated afterwards): a conditional access policy can only react to what has already been evaluated when it applies.

jbnvbzh3lf: The first line is **self-remediation**: a risk-based conditional access policy requires multifactor authentication for a sign-in risk, or a secure password change for a user risk. 2epifzgbxhy: ## What disruption does on its own
21tvv2drvf3: **Automatic attack disruption** correlates Defender XDR signals and uses AI to contain an attack in progress (ransomware, business email compromise, adversary-in-the-middle). On the identity side, three actions stand out. **Disable user** (Defender for Identity) suspends the account to prevent new sign-ins. **Contain user** (Defender for Endpoint) applies a policy on all onboarded devices that blocks the account's inbound traffic in attack protocols (network sign-ins, RPC, SMB, RDP) and ends ongoing remote sessions, **without disabling the account** at the identity provider. A containment triggered by disruption is lifted automatically after **five days**. **Revoke session** and **Suspend user in Entra** cut access on the Entra side. There are also actions for compromised OAuth applications (Defender for Cloud Apps), for AWS (deny policy) and Okta (suspension) through Sentinel.
1ln1ws3ytkr: For an account hosted in **Active Directory**, the disabling goes through the domain controllers running the Defender for Identity sensor. For a synchronized AD account, it also goes through the controllers, and disruption also disables the account in Entra ID. For a **cloud-only** account, the action runs in Entra ID through a Microsoft-managed enterprise application that validates roles. Consequence: without a healthy sensor on a domain controller, disabling an on-premises account can fail. Check sensor health (module 8) before relying on the automation. The containment control requires supported Windows 10 and 11 or Windows Server devices with a sufficient agent version.
1f8iu9kt5bq: In the portal, the incident carries the **Attack Disruption** tag, a yellow banner and the state of the assets (account disabled, device contained); the **Action Center** lists the actions. In advanced hunting, the **DisruptionAndResponseEvents** table gives an organization-wide view. In DeviceEvents, the types containing `ContainedUser` or `ContainedDevice` show the activities **blocked because of** the containment, not the containment itself.
1ugo56py748: ## Exclusions: an exception, not a convenience
1e6qgrjbv1x: Exclusions exist for **user accounts**, **device groups** and **IP addresses** (Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Automated response). Reserve them for critical service accounts, emergency accounts and sensitive infrastructure. Microsoft advises against excluding assets without a reason: an exclusion reduces the effectiveness of disruption against sophisticated attacks. For each exclusion, record the owner, the justification, the review date and a **compensating measure** (dedicated monitoring, reduced privileges). An excluded account that is also a global administrator is a risk, not a solution.

2ef3ipp32mp: An **incident** groups correlated alerts and the associated data that tell the complete story of the attack. An **alert** is an individual signal from a source (Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Identity, Defender for Office 365, Defender for Cloud Apps, Entra ID Protection, custom detections, Sentinel, third-party sources). 1h8sv9y5jck: ## The queue and its priority assistant
24d1zyhw3zo: The queue is under Incidents & alerts > Incidents. The **Queue Assistant** gives each incident a **priority score from 0 to 100** using a machine learning algorithm that takes into account, among other things, attack disruption signals, Threat Analytics, severity, signal-to-noise ratio, MITRE techniques, asset criticality, the rarity of alert types and large-scale threats (ransomware, state actors). Ranges: **red** above 85, **orange** from 15 to 85, **gray** below 15. This score is a triage aid, not a verdict: a gray incident on a domain controller may deserve your attention, and a red one may be a red team exercise. Keep **severity** and **asset criticality** in your columns.
24u4xj0cb6k: By default, the queue shows the last week, new and in-progress incidents, and high, medium and low severities. Build **saved filter sets**: new, high severity unassigned, assigned to me, by tag, by threat category, by associated threat, by source product. Saving a filter's URL gives one-click access. Also filter by **automated investigation state** when you are looking for pending actions. Search accepts the name, the identifier or an involved asset (user, device, mailbox, application).
1oqonhq572v: The **Manage incident** pane lets you: edit the name (the automatic name reflects the number of devices, users and sources), add **tags** that serve as a common language for filters and automation, **assign** (which makes the analyst the owner of the incident and all its alerts), change the status, **classify** and comment. On resolution, you choose a **classification** (true positive, false positive, expected informational activity) and a **determination** (the type of threat). This feeds the team's learning and, depending on the products, the quality of correlation. Resolving an incident resolves the associated alerts in the linked portals.

Avoid bulk resolution without classification: you would lose the only data that lets you measure noise.
